info.description:
Read-only API over eight completed NBA regular seasons (2018-19 to 2025-26) plus the season in progress
(2026-27, season to date, refreshed daily on the local machine) of five-man lineup data, split at the
All-Star break, and the **frozen** Phase 6 model that predicts a lineup's post-break net rating.
Predictions for the season in progress are **provisional** (see `GET /api/v1/data-status` for freshness).

**Read before using predictions**
* A prediction is **conditional**: the expected post-break net rating *if* the lineup plays after the break.
* It uses **pre-break data only**.
* It is **not statistically better than the team-prior baseline**, which is returned with every prediction
  (see `GET /api/v1/model/performance`).
* Uncertainty is large and has two parts: the model's error about the lineup's true quality, and the sampling
  noise of a rating measured over a few dozen to a few hundred possessions.

Ratings are points per 100 possessions. Errors share one shape: `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`.
info.title: NBA Lineup Analytics API

get.description:
Development cross-validation and the one-time held-out evaluation, possession-weighted, with 95%
team-season cluster-bootstrap intervals, and the answer to the pre-registered question: does the model
beat the team prior?

One row per player and team in `season` (a traded player has one row per team). On-court ratings and
on/off come from lineup data; usage from the player endpoint (all teams combined).
Every (season, team) of the player, or only `season`.

post.description:
Predict a lineup given by its five players, including combinations that never played together.

POST because the input is a JSON body, not because anything is created or stored: the call is read-only
and repeatable (same input → same output). If the five already form a recorded lineup, the result equals
GET /lineups/{lineup_id}/prediction.

get.description:
Every qualifying lineup of the season (or team) is ranked before paging, so ranks are global.
`def` ranks the LOWEST defensive rating first; `poss` ranks by own possessions (most used).
Each row carries a sampling SD and a reliability (signal share) so small samples are visible.

in progress, up to the data cutoff), each with the team-prior baseline and 95% intervals. The model is NOT
shown to beat the team-prior baseline, and neighbouring ranks differ by far less than the interval width:
read the order as weak evidence. It predicts quality if played, not playing time.
